impact.derivation: 239 sessions matched the cohort over 11 days (4.2% of this tenant's traffic in the window). Observed resolution 0.314 against a baseline of 0.816 (this cohort has no before-period, so the baseline is other question-answering intents on the same agent in the same window), so 120 conversations that would have resolved did not. 149 ended in a handoff the agent was not built to make; 15 were abandoned. cost_usd is the sum over the cohort and covers v3 traffic only.

findings.if_nothing_changes: At the observed rate this costs about 11 unresolved conversations a day in this cohort, and 62% of them reach a human who was not meant to be involved. The product line is new, so these are first impressions of it.

prescriptions.description: Index the premium card product pack: fees, eligibility, benefits, comparison against the existing gold tier. 11 documents.

decision.asking_approval_for: Index the premium card product pack — 11 documents — into the live knowledge base for the acme-bank agent.
decision.risk_if_diagnosis_wrong: Low. If the cause is not the knowledge gap, we have added correct content the agent did not have; the failure mode is that resolution does not move and we have spent a morning. No existing behaviour changes.
decision.would_not_ship_if: The replay shows any regression on the golden set, or if the premium-card questions turn out to need a policy decision the business has not made yet — in which case the right answer is a scripted handoff, not a knowledge article.

approval.reason: Cheap, reversible, and the evidence is unambiguous — every retrieval in the cohort missed.

prescriptions.description: Assert a non-empty payload with the expected order fields before handing the tool result to the model; on an empty 200, treat it as upstream.malformed_response and take the fallback copy path rather than apologising.

decision.asking_approval_for: Make get_order_status reject an empty 200 as a failure, and take the existing fallback copy path instead of apologising.
decision.risk_if_diagnosis_wrong: Moderate. If some orders legitimately return an empty payload — a very new order, a cancelled one — we would start treating a valid state as an error and route those users to a human unnecessarily. Worth checking with the orders team before shipping.
decision.would_not_ship_if: The empty-payload rate does not fall after the upstream team's own fix lands, which would mean we are patching a symptom on our side of a contract they are about to change again.

approval.reason: Agreed on the diagnosis, but we want the orders team to confirm an empty 200 is never a valid state before we treat it as an error.

gaps.why: No failover mechanism exists in the runtime, so no failover event is ever emitted. There is nothing in the corpus that records a primary path failing and an alternate being chosen, because that choice is never made.
gaps.why_the_proxy_misleads: those are QUALITY retries — the same target re-issued after a malformed response — not a switch to an alternate target. Reporting them as failover would show a small non-zero rate that reads as 'failover is working', when the truth is that failover does not exist. A chart here would be worse than no chart.

gaps.why: Cost per resolved conversation is only computable for v3 traffic — cost_usd lives on llm_call steps, which v2_flow sessions do not emit. On acme-bank that is 27.5% of conversations with no cost attached. We report the v3 figure with the denominator stated rather than a blended number that silently treats a quarter of traffic as free.

self_assessment.notes: One cycle only, so these priors carry no weight yet. With n=1 per change class we report the numbers and explicitly decline to act on them — a hit rate computed from a single observation is not evidence. The loop needs roughly 8-10 cycles per change class before de-weighting anything.
